intended_object: The universal (tautological) point of the standard Borel subgroup B ⊂ SL₂ over a commutative ring R. It is the point of B with values in its own coordinate algebra O(B) that corresponds to the identity map O(B) → O(B) under Yoneda: the "generic" upper-triangular determinant-one matrix with entries in O(B). This reading comes from the docstring and from how the file uses it.
explanation:
The body takes the identity algebra map `AlgHom.id R (coordinateHopfAlgebra R)`. It views this map as an O(B)-valued Hopf-algebra point (`toConv`) and sends it through `pointsMulEquiv`, the library's group isomorphism between A-points of the coordinate Hopf algebra and `SL2Borel A` (upper-triangular matrices of determinant 1 over A). Here A = O(B). By Yoneda, this is exactly the universal point of the functor A ↦ B(A), i.e. the generic Borel matrix.

The library uses it in that role. Its entries define the coordinate functions `diagonalUnit` and `upperRightCoordinate`. It is also the point whose image under the presentation maps is checked to give the isomorphism O(B) ≅ R[T,T⁻¹][X].

The definition works over an arbitrary commutative ring R, which is the natural generality. It is specific to SL₂'s Borel subgroup because that is the object it describes, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has no counterpart, since it does not define this Borel group scheme or its coordinate algebra.
